title: A rank-one generic ideal inclusion
statement: Let $X$ be Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $i:W\to X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $W$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $G$ be a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent] whose stalk at $\xi=i(\operatorname{genericPoint}(W))$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is annihilated by the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$, and has a $\kappa(\xi)$-module structure [def-weil-residue-field] of dimension one compatible with the residue map. There exist a nonzero quasi-coherent ideal $J$ on $W$, represented by $W.\mathrm{IdealSheafData}$, and a monomorphism $\alpha:i_*J\to G$ [def-pc-module-pullback] whose stalk at $\xi$ is invertible. There is no global support hypothesis and no conclusion about cokernels.

proof.text: Apply the generic-point ideal inclusion of Tag 01YE to G and the annihilation hypothesis. It gives a coherent ideal, r summands, and a monomorphism invertible near the generic point. This result is used mathematically; the present library import route through cohomological pushforward is cyclic, so its ideal-lattice construction must be formalized through stalk extension and clearing denominators without that route.

Invertibility on the open neighbourhood gives a bijective generic stalk map. Closed pushforward identifies the source stalk with the finite direct sum of r generic ideal stalks. Zero J or r = 0 gives a zero source, contradicting target dimension one.

For nonzero J its generic inclusion is bijective, so its stalk is the generic local field of W. The closed-immersion surjective local-ring map onto this field has maximal kernel and induces an isomorphism with the ambient residue field. With these identifications the generic map is a residue-field linear isomorphism from r copies of that field to the target line. Mathlib Module.finrank_directSum and invariance under linear equivalence give r = 1.
Identify the single coproduct summand with the ideal. Compose its pushforward isomorphism with the inclusion. Monomorphisms compose, and the generic stalk of the composite is invertible.

lean.statement:
theorem rank_one_generic_ideal_inclusion {X W : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (i : W ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral W]
    (G : X.Modules) (hGcoh : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace G)
    (hGann : ∀ a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk (i.base (genericPoint W))),
      ∀ v : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace
        (i.base (genericPoint W))).obj G, a • v = 0)
    (hGrank : ∃ inst : Module (X.residueField (i.base (genericPoint W)))
      ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace (i.base (genericPoint W))).obj G),
      (∀ (a : X.presheaf.stalk (i.base (genericPoint W)))
        (v : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace
          (i.base (genericPoint W))).obj G),
        a • v = (X.residue (i.base (genericPoint W))) a • v) ∧
      Module.finrank (X.residueField (i.base (genericPoint W)))
        ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace (i.base (genericPoint W))).obj G)
        = 1) :
    ∃ (J : W.IdealSheafData), J ≠ ⊥ ∧
      ∃ (α : (pushforward i).obj J.toModules ⟶ G), Mono α ∧
        IsIso ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace
          (i.base (genericPoint W))).map α)
